title: Circular Stool with Dust Cover
body_html: A boudoir stool designed and created by Heather Greene of ELVN studio, crafted from upcycled SABAI table legs and luxurious SABAI velvet remnants.  A custom Dust Cover was created to accompany the stool for special occasions or safe keeping.

title: Canopy Light
body_html:
In order to reimagine the Sabai City Table Legs I have decided to utilize them as a structural backdrop for a lighting fixture. The design is centered around the existing bolting detail at the top of the legs. The assembly forms a backdrop for a tube light, producing ambient illumination.

The tube light can be oriented up or down, allowing the user to customize the lighting to match the requirements for a space.

title: City Petal Table
body_html:
The City Petal Coffee/Side Table is designed to stand alone or in groups with multiple configurations. Within the endless apartment and home layouts, the City Petal Table can be configured and reconfigured to adapt to your space as needs change. The City Petal Table adapts the strong design language of Sabai's existing City Coffee Table and shifts the orientation of the legs to delicately support a solid Ash wood top by presenting the concave curve outward in contrast to the round top. A small concave bite is taken out of the surface to allow each table to nest against the convex curve of the adjoining table. In line, this procession can go on for as long as one needs. Delightfully, when joining three tables together around a central axis, the petal orientation reveals itself to create a larger coffee table. The final trick of the City Petal Table is that it can be used comfortably as seating in a pinch.

15.5" H x 19.75" L x 18.5" W

title: City Entry Bench
body_html:
The City Entry Bench reimagines Sabai's City table legs as storage underneath a solid Ash wood waterfall bench. As part of the exercise to recontextualize Sabai's existing City table legs, I wanted to investigate opportunities that went beyond using the existing parts as furniture legs. The robust construction and material of the existing pieces led me to discover their use as additional storage. The final design is a balancing act between a delicate wooden bench in harmony with the strong lines and physical weight of the legs, now placed perpendicularly to their intended orientation. To reestablish the visual lightness of the piece, the legs are separated by a specific but crucial gap, playing with the viewer's perception of these pieces floating in space as if they are cantilevered off of the impossibly thin leg. Wherever possible within the design, visual weight is removed to enhance the play between materiality and physical mass.
17.75" H x 31.125" L x 16" W

title: Ko Planter (Second Sundays)
body_html: Ko Planter reimagines Sabai’s City Table steel legs as a planter and miniature landscape, inspired by one of my favorite New York City summer traditions, Second Sundays. On the second Sunday of each month during the summer, LGBTQ+ New Yorkers take over Sheep Meadow in Central Park, laying out in the grass (usually in their skimpy swimwear) and catching up with friends that we haven’t seen in a while. I wanted to capture a little piece of that tradition with handmade ceramic figures lounging around the planter beneath the shade of their own little “tree.” Made with Sabai’s powder-coated steel legs, Baltic birch plywood, and ceramic pieces handmade in Williamsburg. The name Ko means “opening” or “hole” in Chinese, a reference to the circular opening at the center of the piece where this idyllic little landscape comes to life. Follow Max’s ceramics at @hausofmax on Instagram.

title: City Glow
body_html: City Glow reimagines excess steel components from SABAI’s City Table Collection as a sculptural wall sconce. The design gives an existing functional element a new purpose while celebrating the industrial character of the original material. The steel form is paired with a softly diffused light source, creating a warm glow that contrasts with its architectural silhouette.

title: The Stacks
body_html: An upholstered round stool supported on Sabai's reused curved base. Playful in spirit, it takes its cue from tiered cake stands. Banded with different textiles to create the illusion of a stacked cushion, each layer finished with a contrast welt.

title: The Loaf
body_html: A pill-shaped bench reimagined on the same reused curved base. The cushion floats above an open frame with the frame hugging the ends. A plush, rounded silhouette, full like a raised loaf, with nowhere a hard edge.
